title: Retain criterion-based verification definitions
description: Records how identified requirement criteria will be assessed against an exact subject state. It keeps the verification technique, conditions, and expected observations distinct from execution occurrences and actual evidence.
inputs: Requirement and acceptance-criterion basis and intended claim scope.
Assessed subject and state, technique, conditions, expected observations, and authoring provenance.
preconditions: The governed requirement and intended assessment scope are identified.
outputs: Identifiable verification definition with its criterion and subject basis.
Explicit missing or unbound assessment context that prevents treating the definition as complete.
behavior: Retain the criterion basis, exact subject state, technique, conditions, expected observations, and scope supplied by the verification author.
Identify missing subject binding, conditions, or expected outcomes instead of implying that incomplete instructions define a complete assessment.
Preserve the revised definition's basis when it changes so previous observations remain attributable to the definition actually used.
Return the definition as planned method information without producing an execution result or satisfaction conclusion.

failure_behavior.condition: A referenced criterion or assessed subject state cannot be identified.
failure_behavior.outcome: Expose the unresolved basis and prevent a claim of complete assessment definition for that scope.

failure_behavior.condition: A method definition is offered as observed proof without execution evidence.
failure_behavior.outcome: Identify the missing observations and retain the distinction between method and evidence.

sources.basis: SR-025 confirms verification-definition behavior under IR-004; observation recording belongs to FUNC-028.

Propose MOD-007 as the single accountable architectural responsibility for the existing behavior. This allocation preserves the Function definition and does not establish implementation or completed interface/AR coverage outside the IR-001 pilot.
